subject: Post-demo: calibrating first-byte SLA and streaming chunk cadence
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@neptunehealthtech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: calibrating first-byte SLA and streaming chunk cadence

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we have alignment before the pilot: 

What we heard from you:
- Primary product path: real-time chat UI (low interactivity latency) — priority 1.
- Secondary: background summarization for transcripts (throughput-oriented) — priority 2.
- Target initial traffic: ~200 req/s peak, approx 1k messages/day for POC, expected concurrency ~50 active users during peak.

Redwood proposal / questions for calibration:
- TTFT targets: propose two SLO tiers: 
  1) Interactive chat (P1): TTFT <= 120 ms (95th) for short prompts (<= 128 tokens).
  2) Background tasks (P2): TTFT <= 300 ms (95th) acceptable.
- Streaming: recommend SSE as primary (lighter client integration) with WebSocket fallback for mobile/websocket-native clients.
- Chunk cadence: start at 48 tokens per chunk (configurable). We can test 32/64 during the probe to measure visual responsiveness vs. token efficiency.
- Concurrency/throughput: target pilot capacity for 50 concurrent streaming sessions and burst to 250 req/s for 1 minute without degradation.
- Telemetry: we will surface per-request TTFT, chunk size histogram, and per-session packet loss/conn-time metrics.

Attachments: SLA_matrix_neptune_v1.pdf (initial SLO grid), streaming_probe_notes.csv (sample probe config).

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm which TTFT tier is non-negotiable for launch (chat UI target).
2) We run a 48-hour probe with simulated peak patterns (Redwood runs; Neptune provides representative client traces).
3) Joint call to review probe telemetry and pick final chunk cadence + fallback policy (Wednesday preferred).

Can you confirm the P1 TTFT bar and whether SSE + WS fallback is acceptable? If yes, I’ll schedule the probe window and loop Karthik for runbook prep.

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

---

On Sat, 19 Jul 2025 at 16:18 Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@neptunehealthtech.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Hannah — great walkthrough. Two quick clarifications from our side: 
> 
> 1) For the chat UI, our product team is hoping for TTFT closer to 100 ms (95th) on desktop; mobile can be a bit looser. We understand that may require more aggressive batching/priority tuning on your side.
> 2) WebSocket fallback: our mobile SDKs prefer WS and we'd prefer not to add additional SSE plumbing; do you have examples of WS vs SSE feature parity?
> 
> For the POC, ~1k messages/day is accurate. We can provide a replay of typical session traces. Our SRE (engops@neptunehealthtech.com) should be on the probe.
> 
> Can you run a probe that includes a WebSocket path (even if SSE is the default) so we can validate both?
> 
> Jordan
> CTO, Neptune Healthtech
> jordan.lee@neptunehealthtech.com
> 

On Sun, 20 Jul 2025 at 09:12:10 -0700, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hannah / Jordan — looping in a short tech note from infra: 
> 
> - Start with SSE for the initial probe (simpler client logic) but absolutely include a WS route so the mobile SDK can use native WS during the second probe. Redwood runtime supports identical token streaming semantics on both transports; the main differences are: connection multiplexing and client-side heartbeat.
> - TTFT at 100 ms 95th for desktop is ambitious but feasible for short prompts if we: 
>    * Pin a warmed model variant (no cold starts),
>    * Enable KV-prefix caching for common prompt prefixes, and
>    * Use small chunk cadence (32–48 tokens) for the UI path and increase chunk size for background tasks to improve throughput efficiency.
> - Pilot metrics: we recommend measuring TTFT (p50/p95/p99), chunk latency distribution, end-to-end user-perceived time-to-first-character, and server-side queueing.
> - For the SLA matrix I attached a starting grid — Hannah, see SLA_matrix_neptune_v1.pdf in thread. I also put a quick probe config in streaming_probe_notes.csv (rates, concurrency, token distribution).
> 
> Proposed schedule: 48-hour probe starting Wednesday 23 Jul 2025 09:00 PDT. We’ll need Neptune traces by Monday EOD to seed realistic traffic.
> 
> Karthik
> Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
> karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
>
